subject: History
stem: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentence : It may be said that ____ was the founder of Modern Historiography.
solution: Voltaire. The French thinker Voltaire was the first to insist that history must go beyond the deeds of kings, dynasties and wars and take account of the social customs, trade, economy, art and everyday life of ordinary people, and that it must rest on evidence rather than on legend. Because of this rational, comprehensive and evidence-based outlook he is regarded as the founder of modern historiography. Rene Descartes contributed the critical method of testing documents, Leopold von Ranke insisted on the use of original sources, and Karl Marx gave the materialist interpretation of history - important contributions, but none of them founded modern historiography.

subject: History
stem: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentence : ____ is considered as the mother of science and all other subjects.
solution: Philosophy. Philosophy is the systematic enquiry into the ultimate nature of truth, knowledge and existence. Every other branch of learning - the natural sciences, the social sciences and history alike - grew out of that enquiry and separated from it only later, which is why philosophy is described as the mother of science and of all other subjects. Ethics is itself a branch of philosophy, and history and genealogy are individual disciplines, so none of them can hold that place.

subject: History
stem: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentence : Bhilar is known as the village of ____.
solution: Books. Bhilar, a village near Panchgani in Satara district of Maharashtra, was developed by the State Government in 2017 as 'Pustakanche Gaav' - the village of books. Thousands of Marathi books of every kind are kept on display in about twenty-five houses, temples, schools and other buildings of the village, where visitors may sit and read them free of charge. Bhilar has thus become a distinctive centre of literary tourism, the first of its kind in India.

options.label: B

solution: The wrong pair is 'Pandita Ramabai - Stri-Purush Tulana'. Stri-Purush Tulana (1882), the pioneering Marathi tract comparing the condition of men and women, was written by Tarabai Shinde, not by Pandita Ramabai. Rajwade compiled the twenty-two volumes of Marathyanchya Itihasachi Sadhane, V. D. Savarkar wrote The Indian War of Independence 1857, and Mahatma Phule wrote Gulamgiri.

subject: History
stem: Identify the wrong pair in the following and rewrite : (i) Darpan - Balshastri Jambhekar; (ii) Kesari - Bal Gangadhar Tilak; (iii) Deenbandhu - Gopal Hari Deshmukh; (iv) Prabhakar - Bhau Mahajan.
solution: The wrong pair is 'Deenbandhu - Gopal Hari Deshmukh'. Deenbandhu was started in 1877 by Krishnarao Bhalekar, a follower of Mahatma Phule, and was later edited by Narayan Meghaji Lokhande; it voiced the grievances of peasants and mill workers. Gopal Hari Deshmukh 'Lokhitwadi' was not its founder - he wrote his famous Shatapatre in Bhau Mahajan's Prabhakar. Rewritten correctly : Deenbandhu - Krishnarao Bhalekar. The other three pairs are correct - Balshastri Jambhekar began Darpan (1832), the first Marathi newspaper, Lokmanya Tilak began Kesari (1881), and Bhau Mahajan began Prabhakar (1841).

solution:
The completed concept map - Types of Tourism : (1) Historical (heritage) tourism (2) Religious tourism (3) Eco-tourism or nature tourism (4) Health tourism.

Historical tourism takes visitors to forts, caves, monuments and museums; religious tourism to places of pilgrimage such as Pandharpur, Shirdi, Kashi or Ajmer; eco-tourism to forests, sanctuaries, hills and waterfalls where nature is enjoyed without harming it; and health tourism to hot springs, Ayurveda and yoga centres and modern hospitals. Agri-tourism, adventure or sports tourism, cultural tourism and educational tourism are other acceptable answers.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on : Feminist History.
solution: Feminist history, or feminist historiography, is the writing of history from the point of view of women. Traditional history was written almost entirely by men and about men - kings, generals, priests and statesmen - so that half of humanity was left out of the record. Feminist historians argued that the historian's outlook must change: the family, household work, childbirth, marriage customs, women's labour, their property rights and their movements for education and equality must all become subjects of serious historical research. The movement began with the demand for women's suffrage in the West and gathered strength after 1970, when Simone de Beauvoir's 'The Second Sex' made scholars re-examine how the position of women was socially constructed. Feminist history therefore does not merely add women to the old story; it re-writes the story itself by placing gender at the centre of historical enquiry.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on : Need of entertainment.
solution: Human beings cannot work endlessly; after the day's labour the body and the mind both need rest and refreshment, and entertainment provides exactly this. It relieves fatigue and mental strain, restores enthusiasm and makes a person fit for the next day's work. Entertainment is also a social need - festivals, fairs, folk theatre, songs, dances and games bring people together, strengthen the bonds of community and pass on traditions from one generation to the next. It nourishes creativity and gives an outlet to emotions, and forms such as drama, films and literature can educate and awaken society while they amuse it. Because it is thus necessary for the health of both the individual and society, entertainment has existed in every age and in every culture, only its forms have changed with time.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on : Importance of sports.
solution: Sports are important first of all for physical health - regular play keeps the body fit, strong and free from disease and builds stamina. They are equally important for mental health, because a game refreshes the mind, relieves stress and develops concentration, alertness and quick decision-making. Sports build character: a player learns discipline, punctuality, perseverance, team spirit, obedience to rules and the ability to accept both victory and defeat with grace. At the social level games bring together people of different castes, religions, regions and nations, and international events such as the Olympic Games promote friendship and goodwill among countries. Sport has also become a respectable profession today, offering careers as players, coaches, umpires, physiotherapists, commentators and sports journalists, and success in sport brings prestige to the nation.

subject: History
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons : Voltaire said to be the founder of Modern Historiography.
solution: (1) Voltaire, the eighteenth century French philosopher, was the first to declare that history should not be a mere chronicle of kings, dynasties, battles and miracles, and that only facts supported by evidence should be recorded. (2) He widened the very subject-matter of history by insisting that the social customs, trade, economy, agriculture, art, literature and everyday life of ordinary people are as much a part of history as the deeds of rulers. (3) He wrote history with a rational and critical outlook, rejecting religious bias and legend, and his works such as 'The Age of Louis XIV' and 'Essay on the Customs and Spirit of Nations' put this new method into practice. (4) Because this fresh, evidence-based and all-inclusive approach became the foundation of the way history is written today, Voltaire is said to be the founder of modern historiography.

subject: History
subtopic: Conservation and Preservation of Historical Places
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons : The list of World Heritage Sites is announced by UNESCO.
solution: (1) UNESCO - the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation - is the agency of the United Nations charged with protecting the cultural and natural heritage of the whole world. (2) Under its World Heritage Convention of 1972 it identifies places of outstanding universal value, and after examination by expert committees it declares them World Heritage Sites and publishes the list. (3) The purpose of the declaration is to make it the shared responsibility of all nations to conserve such places, because a monument or a natural region of this quality belongs not only to the country in which it stands but to all humanity. (4) A site on the list receives international recognition, technical guidance and financial help for its conservation, and it also attracts tourists from all over the world. Ajanta, Ellora, the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus and the Western Ghats in India are on this list. For all these reasons the list of World Heritage Sites is announced by UNESCO.

subject: History
subtopic: Art, Applied Art and Professional Opportunities
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons : An expert with deep understanding of art history is required in the art market.
solution: (1) In the art market old paintings, sculptures, coins, manuscripts and antiques are bought and sold, and their value depends on their period, style, school and artist - matters that only a student of art history can determine. (2) Such an expert alone can distinguish a genuine work from a forgery or a modern imitation, and can date a work and identify the tradition to which it belongs. (3) He is therefore needed to fix a correct price, to guide collectors, auction houses, galleries and museums in their purchases and to certify what is being sold. (4) He is also required for the proper cataloguing, exhibition, insurance and restoration of art objects and for preventing the illegal trade in stolen antiquities. Hence an expert with a deep understanding of art history is indispensable in the art market.

subject: History
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons : Archives and libraries publish research journals, informative pamphlets, leaflets, posters, etc.
solution: (1) Archives and libraries preserve rare documents, manuscripts, government records, maps, old newspapers and books, and it is their duty not merely to store this material but to make it known and useful to society. (2) By publishing research journals they place before scholars the new material that has come to light and the research based upon it, so that historical knowledge continues to grow. (3) Pamphlets, leaflets, catalogues and guides tell ordinary readers and researchers what an archive or library actually holds, and how, when and on what conditions the material may be consulted. (4) Posters, exhibitions and popular booklets create awareness among the general public - especially students - about the value of documentary heritage and the need to preserve it, and they attract new readers and researchers to the institution. For these reasons archives and libraries undertake such publication work.

subject: History
context:
Read the following extract and answer the questions below :

Dashavatara Theatre : Dashavatara is part of the folk theatre in Maharashtra. Dashavatara shows are presented in the regions of Konkan and Goa after harvesting season is over. The stories presented in these shows are based on the 10 incarnations of Vishnu, namely Matsya, Koorma, Varaha, Narsimha, Wamana, Parashurama, Ram, Krishna, Buddha and Kalki. At the beginning of the show sutradhara, the narrator invokes Lord Ganesha, the destroyer of obstacles.

The method of acting, make-up, costumes in Dashavatara shows is set by the tradition. The show is mostly musical but sometimes there may be a few spontaneous dialogues. The characters representing gods use wooden masks. The show ends by breaking dahihandi, an earthen pot of curds, followed by aarati, singing praises of the God.

In the 18th century Shyamji Naik Kale started a phad, of Dashavatara artists which used to perform all over Maharashtra.

Vishnudas Bhave, the pioneer of Marathi theatre staged mythological plays by introducing some modifications in the Dashavatara style. Thus, the origins of the Marathi theatre can be traced to Dashavatara tradition.
stem: In which state Dashavatara is part of folk theatre ?
solution: Dashavatara is part of the folk theatre of the state of Maharashtra. Its shows are presented chiefly in the Konkan region of Maharashtra and in Goa, after the harvesting season is over.

stem: The form of Dashavatara Folk theatre. Explain.
solution: Dashavatara is a traditional form of folk theatre performed in the Konkan region of Maharashtra and in Goa, and it is staged after the harvesting season is over. Its stories are drawn from the ten incarnations of Lord Vishnu - Matsya, Koorma, Varaha, Narsimha, Wamana, Parashurama, Ram, Krishna, Buddha and Kalki. The performance opens with the sutradhara or narrator invoking Lord Ganesha, the destroyer of obstacles. The style of acting, the make-up and the costumes are all fixed by tradition; the show is mostly musical, though a few spontaneous dialogues may be added, and the actors who play the gods wear wooden masks. It ends with the breaking of the dahihandi, an earthen pot of curds, followed by the aarati sung in praise of the deity. In the eighteenth century Shyamji Naik Kale formed a phad of Dashavatara artists that performed all over Maharashtra, and Vishnudas Bhave, the pioneer of Marathi theatre, staged his mythological plays by modifying this very style - so the origins of the Marathi stage can be traced back to the Dashavatara tradition.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail : What is Marxist History ?
solution:
Marxist history is the school of historical writing founded on the ideas of the German thinker Karl Marx (1818-1883), set out in works such as 'Das Kapital' and 'The Communist Manifesto'.

(1) Marx held that the history of human society is fundamentally the history of the means of production and of the relations of production - that is, of the way in which people produce the goods they need and of the ownership of the means of production.
(2) He argued that society is divided into two classes, the owners of the means of production and the labouring class that has only its labour to sell, and that the exploitation of the second by the first is the central fact of social life.
(3) 'The history of all hitherto existing societies is the history of class struggle' - this conflict between the exploiting and the exploited classes is, in the Marxist view, the driving force of historical change.
(4) Marxist history therefore rejects the older view that history is made by kings, heroes and great men, and studies instead the economic structure, the modes of production such as slavery, feudalism and capitalism, and the condition of workers and peasants.
(5) This approach turned the attention of historians to economic and social history and to the common people, and it deeply influenced later historical writing in Europe and in India.

subject: History
subtopic: Sources of History, their Conservation and Preservation
stem: Answer the following question in detail : What kind of training is required to study written sources ?
solution:
Written sources - inscriptions, copper plates, manuscripts, old letters, revenue records, treaties and government files - cannot simply be picked up and read, and a special training is needed before they can be used as historical evidence.

(1) Training in ancient and medieval scripts, that is palaeography, is essential, because such documents are written in scripts like Brahmi, Kharoshthi and Modi which are no longer in use.
(2) A knowledge of the languages of the documents is equally necessary - Sanskrit, Pali, Prakrit, Ardhamagadhi, Persian, Arabic, Urdu, old Marathi and, for records of the colonial period, English, Portuguese, Dutch or French.
(3) The student must be trained in epigraphy and numismatics to read inscriptions and the legends on coins, and must know the old systems of dating - the Shaka, Vikram, Hijri and Christian eras - so that a document can be correctly placed in time.
(4) He must learn the techniques of source criticism, that is how to test whether a document is genuine, who wrote it, for whom and with what purpose, and how to compare it with other sources before accepting its statements.
(5) Finally he needs training in the proper handling, cleaning, chemical preservation, cataloguing and digitisation of fragile papers, palm-leaf and parchment, and in the archival methods followed in libraries and record offices.

subject: History
subtopic: Art, Applied Art and Professional Opportunities
stem: Answer the following question in detail : What kind of professional opportunities are available in the field of arts ? Explain.
solution:
The field of art today offers a very wide range of careers, both in the fine arts and in the applied arts.

(1) In the visual arts a person may become a painter, sculptor, potter, wood or metal craftsman, or a designer of textiles, jewellery and pottery, and may exhibit and sell his own work.
(2) In the applied and commercial arts there is a great demand for graphic designers, illustrators, cartoonists, animators, photographers, film and video editors, advertising and web designers, interior decorators, fashion designers and stage-set designers.
(3) In the performing arts one may take up a career as a singer, instrumentalist, dancer, actor, director, choreographer, music composer, sound recordist or light designer in theatre, films, television and the recording industry.
(4) Teaching and research offer another line - art teachers in schools and colleges, teachers in music and dance academies, and research scholars in art history and aesthetics.
(5) Art institutions need curators and guides for museums and art galleries, conservators and restorers of old paintings and sculptures, art critics and journalists, and experts and valuers for the art market and auction houses.
(6) Art therapy, art management, event organisation and the marketing of handicrafts through emporia and online platforms are newer opportunities.

Thus a student who trains himself in art can earn both a good living and social respect.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail : What were the different means of communication known around the world before the advent of Newspaper ?
solution:
Long before newspapers appeared, people had devised many ways of sending news and messages from one place to another.

(1) The oldest and simplest means was word of mouth - messengers, runners and heralds carried news from village to village, and travellers, traders, pilgrims and soldiers spread it along their routes.
(2) Rulers employed royal messengers and a horse and camel post; in India the dak-chowki system and the daroga of the post, and in the Roman empire the cursus publicus, carried official despatches over long distances.
(3) In towns and villages the news of royal orders was announced publicly by the beating of a drum - the dawandi or dvandi - and by criers, while inscriptions on stone and copper plates and edicts set up in public places, like those of Emperor Ashoka, made royal decisions permanently known.
(4) Written letters were sent by hand, and carrier pigeons were trained to fly with small messages; in the Sahyadri and other hill regions signals were passed from fort to fort by lighting fires or by blowing horns, and smoke signals and beacon lights were used in many countries.
(5) Fairs, markets, temples, mosques and village squares, and the songs of bards, powadas, kirtans, folk plays and ballads, were the popular channels through which events were narrated to large numbers of people.

The invention of printing by Gutenberg in the fifteenth century changed this situation, and it became possible to circulate the same news in the same words to thousands of readers - which led to the newspaper.

subject: Political Science
subtopic: Right to Vote and Adult Suffrage
stem: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the statement : The essence of democracy is ____.
solution: Universal adult franchise. Democracy means the rule of the people, and the people can rule only if every adult citizen has the right to choose the government. The Indian Constitution therefore granted the vote to every citizen who has completed 18 years of age, without any distinction of caste, religion, sex, property or education. It is this equal right to vote that makes the government answerable to the people and gives every citizen an equal share in political power; hence universal adult franchise is called the essence or the soul of democracy. Decentralisation of power, reservation of seats and judicial decisions all strengthen democracy, but they follow from it rather than constitute its essence.

subject: Political Science
stem: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the statement : ____ is the main demand of farmers movement.

options.label: A
options.text: Right to cultivate on the forest land

options.label: B
options.text: To get the right price for agricultural product

solution: To get the right price for agricultural product. The farmers' movement in India arose because the cultivator did not receive a remunerative price for what he grew, while the cost of seeds, fertilisers, water and electricity kept rising. Its central demand has therefore always been a fair and guaranteed price for agricultural produce, along with the waiving of debts, cheaper credit and inputs, and protection from the exploitation of middlemen. The right to cultivate forest land is the demand of the tribal movement, protection of consumers is the demand of the consumer movement, and the building of dams is a demand associated with irrigation projects, often opposed by displaced people's movements.

subject: Political Science
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false. Give reasons for your answer : Indian democracy is considered the largest democracy in the world.
solution:
True.

Reasons : (1) India has the largest electorate in the world - about ninety crore voters - and no other democratic country conducts elections on such a scale. (2) The Constitution grants universal adult franchise, so every citizen who has completed 18 years of age votes without any distinction of caste, religion, sex, language, property or education. (3) Elections are held regularly and peacefully to the Lok Sabha, the State Legislative Assemblies and lakhs of seats in the local self-government bodies, and crores of people take part in them. (4) India is also a democracy of remarkable diversity, with many religions, languages, castes and regions living together under one Constitution, and it has kept its democratic system working without a break since 1947. For all these reasons Indian democracy is considered the largest democracy in the world.

subject: Political Science
subtopic: Characteristics and Functions of Political Parties
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false. Give reasons for your answer : Political parties act as a link between government and people.
solution:
True.

Reasons : (1) Political parties gather the demands, opinions and grievances of the people, put them together in their programmes and manifestos, and place them before the government, so that public opinion reaches those in power. (2) They explain the policies, laws and schemes of the government to the people through their workers, meetings, publications and the media, so that the citizens understand what the government is doing. (3) The party in power forms the government and carries out the promises made to the voters, while the opposition parties criticise the government, expose its failures and compel it to answer for its actions - both roles keep the government responsive to the people. (4) Parties also give political education to the citizens, prepare public opinion at election time and offer the voter a choice of candidates and programmes. Because they thus carry the wishes of the people to the government and the decisions of the government back to the people, political parties are rightly said to be a link between the government and the people.

subject: Political Science
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false. Give reasons for your answer : Importance of the problems of farmers and tribals has increased in the left extremist movement.
solution:
True.

Reasons : (1) The left extremist movement grew in the forest and hill districts of central and eastern India, which are inhabited mainly by tribals and poor peasants, and it took up their unsettled problems as its own. (2) Landlessness, the exploitation of tenants and agricultural labourers, indebtedness, the loss of tribal land to moneylenders and contractors, denial of rights over forest produce and displacement by mines and big projects had not been solved by the ordinary political process. (3) The movement therefore raised the demands of land to the tiller, restoration of tribal land, forest rights and fair wages, and won support among these very sections by promising them justice. (4) The failure of governmental development and rehabilitation schemes to reach these remote areas increased the discontent, and the extremists used it to strengthen their hold. Hence it is true that the problems of farmers and tribals have gained importance in the left extremist movement.

subject: Political Science
stem: Explain the following concept : Right to Information.
solution: The Right to Information is the right of every citizen to obtain information about the working of the government and of public authorities. It was given legal shape by the Right to Information Act of 2005, under which a citizen may apply to the information officer of any government office, department, public undertaking or aided institution and ask for records, files, documents, orders, accounts or reports, and the officer is bound to supply the information within a fixed period, usually thirty days. Only a few matters, such as those affecting the security and sovereignty of the country, are exempted. The purpose of the right is to make the administration transparent and accountable, to check corruption, favouritism and the misuse of public money, and to enable the ordinary citizen to know how decisions that affect him are taken. It has thus become an important instrument for deepening democracy and for making the government truly answerable to the people.

subject: Political Science
stem: Explain the following concept : Regionalism.
solution: Regionalism means an excessive attachment to one's own region, state or linguistic area, in which the interest of that region is placed above the interest of the nation as a whole. It arises out of differences of language, culture and geography and, more importantly, out of the uneven development of different regions - when a region feels that it has been neglected in the matter of industry, irrigation, employment or the sharing of river water and funds, a feeling of injustice grows there. Regionalism expresses itself in demands for separate statehood, in disputes over boundaries and river waters, in agitations for reserving jobs for 'sons of the soil' and sometimes in hostility towards people who have come from other states. A healthy regional consciousness that seeks the balanced development of a backward area is not harmful, but when it turns into narrow and aggressive parochialism it weakens national unity and integration and becomes a serious challenge to Indian democracy.

stem: Do as instructed - complete the following concept diagram. The centre box of the printed diagram reads 'National Parties in India'; four boxes are joined to it - one above, one on the left, one on the right and one below - and all four are blank. Write the name of an appropriate national party in each of the four blank boxes.
solution:
The completed concept diagram - National Parties in India : (1) Indian National Congress (2) Bharatiya Janata Party (3) Bahujan Samaj Party (4) Communist Party of India (Marxist).

A party is recognised as a national party by the Election Commission when it satisfies the prescribed conditions of votes and seats in several states. The Nationalist Congress Party, the Communist Party of India and the All India Trinamool Congress are other acceptable answers.

subject: Political Science
stem: Do as instructed - complete the following concept diagram. The centre box of the printed diagram reads 'Democratic Values'; four boxes are joined to it - one above, one on the left, one on the right and one below - and all four are blank. Write an appropriate democratic value in each of the four blank boxes.
solution:
The completed concept diagram - Democratic Values : (1) Liberty or freedom (2) Equality (3) Fraternity or brotherhood (4) Justice.

These are the values proclaimed in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution. Liberty means freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; equality means equality of status and of opportunity for all citizens; fraternity means the spirit of brotherhood that assures the dignity of the individual and the unity of the nation; and justice means social, economic and political justice. Secularism, tolerance and respect for the dignity of the individual are other acceptable answers.

subject: Political Science
stem: Answer in brief : What is code of conduct ? Explain.
solution:
The code of conduct is the set of rules laid down by the Election Commission which every political party, candidate and the government in power must observe from the day the election programme is announced until the results are declared. Its purpose is to ensure that the election is free and fair and that no party is able to take an unfair advantage over another.

Under the code a candidate may not appeal to voters in the name of caste, religion or language, nor create hatred between communities; he may not bribe or intimidate voters, use money and muscle power, or hold meetings and processions without the permission of the authorities. Loudspeakers may not be used after the prescribed hours, and the expenditure of a candidate must not exceed the limit fixed by the Commission. The ruling party may not use government vehicles, offices, machinery or funds for its campaign, and it may not announce new schemes, grants or appointments once the code has come into force.

The code of conduct is thus an important means of keeping the electoral process clean, orderly and impartial.

subject: Political Science
stem: Answer in brief : For which reforms were the women's movement in the pre-independence period fighting ?
solution:
In the period before independence the women's movement in India was closely linked with the social reform movement, and it fought mainly for the removal of the social evils that kept women in a state of subjection.

Its chief demands were : (1) education for girls and women, which the reformers regarded as the first condition of their progress; (2) abolition of the custom of sati and of child marriage, and the fixing of a minimum age of marriage; (3) permission for widows to remarry, and an end to the cruel treatment and disfigurement of widows; (4) an end to polygamy and to the devadasi system, and relief for deserted women; (5) legal rights for women in property and inheritance, and reform of the laws of marriage and divorce; (6) the right to vote and to contest elections, and a share in public and political life.

Reformers such as Raja Rammohan Roy, Mahatma Jotirao Phule and Savitribai Phule, Maharshi Karve, Pandita Ramabai and Ramabai Ranade, and organisations like the Bharat Mahila Parishad and the All India Women's Conference, led this struggle, and many of these demands were secured through laws passed in this period and after independence.
